main_results.summary: Three-runner: TAGS+TimeRanges 50000 old+live vs clean 2000 active, same SAMPLES 2000; native reads17x rows, 17.38x bytes, broad wall+42.75% CPU+46.2%, project_p0 wall+28.3% CPU+32.5%. Old samples manually dropped in this performance test.
Actual SAMPLES INNER 30d TTL preserves old TAGS+TimeRanges; late expired sample removed; resuming original ID writes fresh sample and becomes visible with unchanged TAGS count.
16 repeated expired inserts, real TTL and natural maintenance; zero-row part count cyclic1→2→3→4→1 and bytes1244→4976→1244, no old sample rows; not long-run HA guarantee.

Direct inner TAGS delete with warm dedup cache: new SAMPLES inserted but no TAGS row, native output invisible; cache-disabled control restores visibility. Table-scoped SYSTEM DROP TIME SERIES CACHES + further INSERT recovers; actual source documents this caveat.

After old SAMPLES TTL, direct cleanup of only obsolete TimeRanges rows preserves exact current native output and old TAGS IDs; fresh old-ID insertion recreates TimeRanges even with cache warm; no races tested.

Same 50000 TAGS, 2000 live SAMPLES and source; 50000 vs2000 TimeRanges native ABBA, read_rows102000→54000, compressed read7.894→5.974MB but broad wall p50 -2.0%, CPU-4.8%, exact project wall+3.5% (regression). Cleanup mutation costs not counted; reject standalone optimization.

next_proven_knowledge: No simple inner-TAGS DELETE (invisible fresh samples on cache hits) and no blanket TimeRanges-only cleanup performance win. Metadata retention contributes to high-cardinality read cost; current R07 owner is independently testing active ID access paths, so coordinate rather than launch duplicate index experiments. Real production-SLA decision still requires matched optimized ClickHouse vs VictoriaMetrics and realistic 14d/1.33m high churn.
safety_stop: Do not change master, production, scheduler or TTL defaults. Do not deploy direct metadata deletion without atomic writer/replica-cache coordination, source-level late/backfill/ID correctness, and a net CPU/write cost model. Do not claim any pure jemalloc gain from patched O1 binary (R18 owns the confounded 4992-query capacity gate).
summary: R19 retention cost and safety investigation: 3-runner 17x extra metadata row scans and 42.8% broad native p50 wall cost; actual TTL/resurrection semantic proof; direct TAGS GC unsafe under cache, and TimeRanges-only cleanup failed meaningful CPU/wall gate.
